text: Yes, Mr. Mayor, I think this is procedural. As the report indicates, due to the COVID situation, the general elections for councils have been postponed for 12 months. So, we now need to map out our meeting arrangements, as indicated, for the next six months, and then we'll reassess and move beyond that. I have one question. It relates to the fact that on page 106, halfway down, it says due to COVID-19 pandemic, council has continued to meet remotely to meet the public health orders. Well, I thought there'd been orders issued by the minister that councils could resume face-to-face meetings again. So, I was just wondering, through you, Mr. Mayor, if the general manager could clarify the current status in terms of the minister and his allowance for councils to get back to face-to-face.

speaker: clrirmarkbennett
text: Thank you, general manager.

speaker: markbennettmayor
text: So, what has the minister for local government, councillor, it's to do with the public health orders where four metres per person square required, and 1.5 metre distance between people in the room. So, we did discuss this with the councillors, the option of holding the

speaker: clrirmarkbennett
text: council meeting in the large hall to meet those spatial requirements, but the logistics of doing

speaker: markbennettmayor
text: that were seen to be prohibitive, and with people or members of the public wishing to address council, they can now do that through Zoom, and that was seen to be acceptable. So, the key issue, councillor, is the four metres square per person plus the 1.5 metre distance between attendees.

speaker: rosswilliams
text: But that can be achieved, Mr. Mayor, through you. The question is that my calculation is that the council chamber is 74 square metres. That can accommodate under the four square metre rule, 18 people, and we only need 12 people at a council meeting. We can distribute people around the room to meet the 1.5 without any difficulty. So, I don't personally accept that we shouldn't be having face-to-face, but that seems to be the desire of the general manager, but I think the rules would allow us to do it if we were a bit creative. But anyway, I think it's important that we get our meeting dates out in the public so that we can continue our process, whether it's remotely or whether it's face-to-face. But I would like to see us get back to face-to-face

speaker: markbennettmayor
text: as soon as possible. It wasn't a decision of the general manager, it was a decision of the council as we discussed it. We did a poll. There were very few people who wanted to get back together just yet. There is still a heightened concern about COVID-19. I think it behooves us to be as careful as we can. In any of our dealings, it's caused me a great deal of concern. I see my responsibility is to keep people in the municipality safe. As you know, it's been suggested to me I drop off mentioning COVID-19 in the mayoral column. I won't. I'm going to keep pursuing it. I think it's a real issue. When I look at what's happening in Victoria, I'm convinced we just need to be very cautious. So, could I encourage you all to be very cautious? The decision was made by councillors who voted informally to continue the meetings the way we're having at the moment. So, it wasn't the general manager's idea. General manager, anything you'd like to add to that?
